task.title: Configure Radware DefensePro on an Intra-Chassis Cluster

li.p:
Download the vDP image from Cisco.com (see ) and then uploaddownload that image to the
(see ).

context.p: The following procedure shows how to install the Radware DefensePro image, and configure it in a Service Chain in front of an ASA or Firepower Threat Defense intra-chassis cluster.

note.p: Service Chaining is not supported in an inter-chassis cluster configuration. However, the Radware DefensePro application can be deployed in a standalone configuration in an inter-chassis cluster scenario.

step.cmd: If you want to use a separate management interface for vDP, enable the interface and set it to be the mgmt type according to . Otherwise, you can share the application management interface.
Configure an ASA or Firepower Threat Defense intra-chassis cluster (see or ).

info.p: Note that before you click Save at the end of the procedure to configure the intra-chassis cluster, you must first follow the following steps to add a vDP decorator to the cluster.

step.cmd: In the Decorators area, select vDP. The Radware: Virtual DefensePro - Configuration dialog box appears. Configure the following fields under the General Information tab.
If you have more than one vDP version uploaded to the , select the vDP version you want to use in the Version drop-down.

If you have a resource configurable Radware DefensePro application, a list of supported resource profiles appears under the Resource Profile drop-down. Select the resource profile you want to assign to the device. If you do not select a resource profile, the default setting is used.
Under the Management Interface drop-down, choose a management interface.
Click the checkbox next to each data port that you want to assign to the vDP decorator.
Click the Interface Information tab.
Select the Address Type to be used, IPv4 only, IPv6 only, or IPv4 and IPv6.
Configure the following fields for each Security Module. Note that the fields that display depend on your Address Type selection from the previous step.

substep.cmd: In the Management IP field, configure a local IP address.
IPv4 only: Enter a Network Mask.

info.p: IPv6 only: Enter a Prefix Length.

step.cmd: Click OK.
Click Save.

info.p:
The
deploys the logical device by downloading the specified software version and pushing the bootstrap configuration and management interface settings to the specified security module.

step.cmd: Choose Logical Devices to open the Logical Devices page.
Scroll through the list of configured logical devices to the entries for vDP. Verify their Attributes listed in the Management IP column.

choices.choice: If the CLUSTER-ROLE element displays as unknown for the DefensePro instances, you must enter the DefensePro application and configure the master IP address to complete the creation of the vDP cluster.
If the CLUSTER-ROLE element displays as primary or secondary for the DefensePro instances, the applications are online and formed in a cluster.

step.cmd: If you want to use a separate management interface for vDP, enable the interface and set it to be the mgmt type according to . Otherwise, you can share the application management interface.
Configure an ASA intra-chassis cluster (see ) or a Firepower Threat Defense intra-chassis cluster (see ).

step.cmd: (Optional) Set the resource profile using one of the available profiles from the previous step:

note.p: After committing this change, the FXOS chassis reboots.

step.cmd: Configure cluster port channel:

info.p: enter external-port-link port-channel48 Port-channel48 { asa | ftd }

step.cmd: Configure management bootstrap for all three DefensePro instances:

stepxmp.codeblock:
enter mgmt-bootstrap vdp enter ipv4 1 default set gateway 172.16.0.1 set ip 172.16.4.219 mask 255.255.0.0 exit
enter ipv4 2 default set gateway 172.16.0.1 set ip 172.16.4.220 mask 255.255.0.0 exit
enter ipv4 3 default set gateway 172.16.0.1 set ip 172.16.4.221 mask 255.255.0.0 exit

step.cmd: Exit management bootstrap configuration scope:
Enter the DefensePro application instance on the master blade:
On the master blade, set the management IP:
Using the IP found in the previous step, set the master IP:
Enable the cluster:
Exit the application console and return to the FXOS module CLI:
Repeat steps 10, 12, 13, and 14 to set the master IP found in step 11 and enable the cluster for each blade application instance.
Commit the configuration:

info.note: After completing this procedure, you must verify whether the DefensePro instances are configured in a cluster.

step.cmd: Validate that all DefensePro applications have joined the cluster:
Use either of the following methods to verify which DefensePro instance is primary, and which one is secondary.

substep.cmd: Scope the DefensePro instance and show appplication attributes for DefensePro only:
Scope the slot and show the DefensePro instance in expanded detail. This approach displays information for both logical device and vDP application instances on the slot.

result.p: If the DefensePro application is online but not yet formed in a cluster, the CLI displays: App Attribute: App Attribute Key: cluster-role Value: unknown
If the system displays this "unknown" value, you must enter the DefensePro application and configure the master IP address to create the vDP cluster.
If the DefensePro application is online and formed in a cluster, the CLI displays: App Attribute: App Attribute Key: cluster-role Value: primary/secondary

enter ipv4 2 default set gateway 172.16.0.1 set ip 172.16.4.220 mask 255.255.0.0 exit

taskbody.postreq: Set a password for the DefensePro application. Note that the application does not come online until you set a password. For more information, see the Radware DefensePro DDoS Mitigation User Guide on cisco.com.
